reports.title: CVS HEALTH CORPORATION REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTSAND RAISES FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE

desk.headline: Revenue up 5% to $108.4bn and adjusted EPS of $2.09 beat; full-year 2026 guidance raised again

other.label: GAAP diluted EPS
other.change: vs loss of $3.13 a year ago

results: Sales rose 5.4% to $108.4bn; adjusted EPS climbed to $2.09 from $1.60, while GAAP EPS was $1.68 against a loss a year ago that included a $5.7bn goodwill write-down.
Aetna's insurance arm drove the gain: adjusted operating profit nearly tripled to $912m and the medical benefit ratio improved to 91.3% from 92.8%, mainly in government plans.
The pharmacy benefit unit grew sales 9.5% to $54.0bn but profit only 2.7%; the retail pharmacy unit's sales fell 2% while its adjusted profit rose 10.6% to $1.6bn.
Medical membership held at 26.1m versus June; over 69% of Medicare Advantage members are in 2027 plans rated 4 stars or higher.
Operating cash flow reached $15.3bn for the nine months; a $193m charge for an Omnicare guarantee was excluded from adjusted results.

guidance.summary: CVS raised its 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to at least $8.20 and lifted cash-flow guidance by $4bn, while keeping a cautious stance on high medical costs. On the call, as reported, it also gave an early 2027 floor of at least $8.65 adjusted EPS.

points: Management plans to split CVS into two listed companies by the first half of 2028: CVS Pharmacy (stores, mail order, MinuteClinic) and a company keeping Aetna, Caremark and the care businesses.
Medical cost trends stayed high but roughly as expected; management expects elevated trend to persist through 2027 and said Medicare Advantage turned profitable in 2026.
Caremark (pharmacy benefits) profit is expected to bottom in 2027 at no less than $7bn, hurt by lower 340B income and a softer selling season.
Leverage targets were reached early, so share buybacks restart in Q4; both future companies are meant to keep investment-grade balance sheets.
GLP-1 prescription volume rose 23% at retail pharmacies, per the call coverage.
call.source: Call coverage: Zacks (via TradingView) and MarketBeat (via Yahoo Finance), 4–5 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Details and costs of the planned pharmacy separation, and how the two companies are capitalised.
Whether medical cost trends at Aetna stay in line with plans as 2027 pricing takes effect.
Formal 2027 guidance on the Q4 call, including the Caremark earnings trough.
